ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (97) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

Chekhov's story as Tolstoy printed it, translated closely from this Russian text: «душечка» (dushechka, 'darling') is 'darling' throughout, and Olenka's echoed opinions keep the wording of the men she repeats. The garbled telegram keeps its errors: «хохороны» (khokhorony, for похороны, 'funeral') is 'huneral' and the meaningless «сючала» (syuchala) is left transliterated; Sasha's childish «ощенится» (oshchenitsya, 'has puppies') of the cat is kept.
Source observation: [41] «…до лестницы, — Спасибо…»: a capital letter after the comma inside Olenka's speech (probably a period was meant); rendered as one continuing sentence.
Source observation: [67] the speech dash before «Когда она у вас ощенится» is missing, though Sasha plainly goes on speaking; the English supplies the dash.
